text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government has launched an investigation into alleged discrepancies in a contract issued by Telekom Malaysia Bhd to Sweden's Ericsson group.
-- Malaysia has banned the British freighter Pacific Teal, which is carrying processed nuclear waste, from using its waterways.

-- The Sapura Group is not the only company eyeing a stake in motor distributor UMW Holdings Bhd, currently held by the state savings fund, Permodalan Nasional Bhd, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Wednesday.
-- Financial supermarket AMMB Holdings Bhd, part of the Arab-Malaysian Group of companies, will begin stock and derivatives trading in Hong Kong next month said group chairman Azman Hashim.
-- Finance authorities need not intervene in the movement of the ringgit, as the currency had been strong and stable over the past year, said Anwar.
